cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Gratitude – the feeling of being thankful and showing appreciation.

p.em: Example: Showing sincere gratitude can make a huge difference in your relationships.

cosy-blockquote.p: Appreciation ≠ Indifference – the recognition of the good qualities of someone ≠ a total lack of interest or concern.

p.em: Example: We must show deep appreciation for our teachers instead of cold indifference.

cosy-blockquote.p: Connection – a positive relationship or link between people.

p.em: Example: There is a strong connection between sharing meals and building a happy community.

cosy-blockquote.p: Spontaneous – done in a sudden, natural way without planning.

p.em: Example: Our spontaneous coffee meeting turned out to be the highlight of my week.

cosy-blockquote.p: Gesture – an action that expresses a feeling or intention.

p.em: Example: Holding the door open for an elderly person is a small but kind gesture.

cosy-blockquote.p: Generosity – the quality of being kind, helpful, and giving to others.

p.em: Example: Her generosity was clear when she offered to help us move our heavy furniture.

cosy-blockquote.p: Impact – a powerful effect or influence on a situation or person.

p.em: Example: A supportive coworker can have a major impact on your job satisfaction.

cosy-blockquote.p: Genuine ≠ fake – real, honest, and sincere; not fake.

p.em: Example: He offered a genuine apology for arriving late to our dinner.

cosy-blockquote.p: Support – to give help, encouragement, or approval to someone.

p.em: Example: My parents always support my career decisions.

cosy-blockquote.p: Uplift – to make someone feel happier, more hopeful, or more positive.

p.em: Example: Her funny stories always uplift my mood when I am feeling down.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Who is someone who has played a major role in your life, and what did they do to help you?
★ Do you find it easy to express gratitude to people in your daily life?

Why is a handwritten letter that comes in the mail so much more powerful than a digital text?
★ When was the last time you wrote a physical letter to someone?

How does buying a gift to celebrate a friend's success strengthen your relationship?
★ Do you prefer giving gifts or receiving them?

Is there a specific holiday that you use to remember and honor important people in history?
★ What is your favorite holiday for spending time with loved ones?

What is an active gesture whoever wants to show kindness can use to make a stranger smile?
★ Have you ever made a random stranger smile with a small gesture?

Who is a hero who inspired you when you were growing up, and what did they do to change your views?
★ Do you think we have enough real heroes in the media today?

Why is gratitude a habit that we need to practice daily to keep our minds happy?
★ What are three simple things you are grateful for today?

What is a tradition that your community uses to support lonely neighbors during winter?
★ Are there any special charity traditions in your neighborhood?

Why is kindness a language that everyone can understand, and how can we use it to unite people?
★ How do you teach kindness to younger children?

Who is a teacher who went out of their way to guide you when you were struggling at school?
★ Do you still stay in touch with any of your former teachers?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: 💌 Activity 1: The Wall of Gratitude Expressing appreciation strengthens human bonds. Together with your partner, choose a person whom you want to thank today. Draft a short, heartfelt thank-you card to them. Practice using relative clauses (the person who..., the help that...) and infinitives of purpose (to say..., to support...): 👩‍🏫 An Unsung Teacher The guide who worked tirelessly to help you build confidence and learn. 💼 A Supportive Coworker The peer who offered help on a hectic task to ensure you met the deadline. 🏡 A Caring Neighbor The neighbor who keeps your keys to protect your home when you travel. 🏆 Closing: The Honorary Tribute If you could establish an official public monument to celebrate one category of unsung heroes, who would you choose to honor today? 🧹 Neighborhood Cleaners & Caretakers 🚴 Spontaneous Delivery Riders & Couriers ❤️ Dedicated Local Charity Volunteers 🚌 Helpful Public Bus & Train Drivers

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, we will use AI systems that analyze our relationships to schedule mandatory appreciation days.
★ Would you want an AI to tell you when gratitude is required?

The act of sending a physical letter, which requires time and effort to write, will become completely extinct.
★ Would you miss physical mail if everything became digital to save paper?

A global holiday that is designed to force people to be kind will backfire, making kindness feel fake.
★ Can you force someone to show genuine appreciation?

Virtual reality will allow us to send a digital gift that uses sensory feedback to simulate a real hug.
★ Would a virtual hug be enough to make you feel loved?

We will have a robotic hero that performs dangerous tasks to protect human lives in emergencies.
★ Would you trust a robot to rescue you from a burning building?

Future schools will introduce classes in gratitude that use biometric bands to track sincerity.
★ Is sincerity something that technology can measure?

A simple gesture that is captured on video will become a form of social currency to buy popularity.
★ Have you ever shared a kind act on social media to get likes?

The ancient tradition of family gatherings, which people use to bond, will be replaced by neural connections.
★ Would you prefer a neural connection to share thoughts instantly with family?

We will have a specialized city department that employs professional actors to spread kindness in public spaces.
★ Would public kindness feel different if you knew the person was paid to do it?

A digital teacher that is programmed to understand your emotions will replace human educators.
★ Can a computer program have the empathy that is needed to teach children?

ul.li: Incorrect: I am very grateful of my teacher. → Correct: I am very grateful to my teacher / grateful for my teacher's help. ((Preposition check: 'grateful' is followed by 'to' for people, and 'for' for actions/things.))
Incorrect: We discussed about our someone special. → Correct: We discussed our special someone. ((Preposition error: the verb 'discuss' is transitive and does not take 'about'.))
Incorrect: It is very important to nurturing friendships. → Correct: It is very important to nurture friendships. ((Infinitive structure: 'to' is followed by the base form of the verb 'nurture'.))
